research.report: Research report: 'The Potential Dividend Compounder: Rising Yield, Defensible Earnings' (HNB Stockbrokers, November 2026)
keyPoints: Consolidation (Airtel Lanka bought in 2024; three mobile operators instead of four, mobile HHI up from 3,142 in 2020 to 4,629) gives Dialog, with over 60% of mobile, pricing power and scale; EBITDA margin was 51.9% on a trailing basis vs 42.0% for regional peers.

Margin gains now come from spreading a largely fixed network cost over more revenue rather than cutting variable costs; lower depreciation (27% of revenue in FY25 to about 25% in FY27E) adds to EBIT margin.

Revenue growth slows to about 5% a year (FY25–FY28E) and is ARPU-led: mobile subscribers about +1% a year, mobile ARPU about +3% a year from FY27E, fixed broadband ARPU +2% rising to +4%, pay-TV ARPU below +2% as streaming bites. EBITDA grows about 10% a year.

Capex rises with 5G to a peak of about 21% of revenue in FY28E, then eases; free cash flow to equity stays around Rs 50bn a year, so the payout rises from about 70% to over 80% and net debt/EBITDA falls from about 0.7x to about 0.4x by FY27E.

Valuation: 10-year DCF gives Rs 59.49 a share (enterprise value Rs 598.9bn, less debt Rs 77.3bn plus cash Rs 30.1bn); cost of equity 16.0% (11.0% five-year bond yield, beta 1.0, 5.0% premium), pre-tax cost of debt 10.5%, 35:65 debt:equity, WACC 12.97%, terminal growth 5.0%. Sensitivity range Rs 55.51–63.80 (±1 point on WACC and terminal growth); peer multiples (P/E, EV/EBITDA, EV/sales) give higher ranges.

news.title: IMF board to take up Sri Lanka's seventh review on 2 Dec
news.text: Approval would release about $345mn under the $2.9bn programme, which ends in March 2027; the review includes waivers and changes to performance criteria. A committee is studying a follow-up arrangement (a funded Stand-By Arrangement or a Policy Coordination Instrument are options). Foreign debt service is about $3bn in 2027 and $3.6bn in 2028; reserves are about $7bn, and growth is projected at 4% in 2027.

news.title: Credit growth slows to 21.8% but stays high
news.text: Since May's 100bps hike, the call money rate is up 108bps, the one-year T-bill 146bps and the weekly prime lending rate 166bps, yet private credit still grows about 21.8% a year, which helped prompt last week's second hike. The Governor named personal loans, pawning and financial services as the fastest-growing areas, defended the 70% loan-to-value cap on gold loans, and said the deposit-rate cap on finance companies stays.

news.title: Central Bank to get tradeable bonds to soak up liquidity
news.text: From March 2027 the step-down coupons on the Central Bank's restructured government bonds end and they become ordinary 5% fixed-rate bonds, which it can sell at a discount to drain excess rupees from banks instead of issuing its own securities or raising reserve requirements.

news.title: Sinopec's Hambantota refinery stalls
news.text: The proposed $3.7bn, 200,000-barrel-a-day refinery has stalled after Sinopec withdrew over market access and tax relief; there is no penalty as no letter of intent was signed. Options include a joint venture with Lanka IOC, a PPP tender, and the Sapugaskanda refinery upgrade (expressions of interest shortlisted). The Energy Minister wants two more months to decide.

news.title: Construction support centre ahead of Rs 2tn development budget
news.text: The 'Builders' Gateway' centre, under the Presidential Secretariat, will help contractors and suppliers resolve tender, contract and administrative problems free of charge as the Government prepares a Rs 2tn development budget for 2027; about 95% of public project work is done by the private sector.

news.title: Minimum export prices planned for coconut charcoal and fresh nuts
news.text: The Coconut Development Authority will set minimum declared export prices rather than ban exports: fresh nuts from about $0.40 to $0.70–0.80 a nut, and a floor (not yet announced) for shell charcoal, now exported at $300–330/t while local activated carbon makers import it at about $380/t. Government approval is pending.

news.title: Tourist arrivals pass 2 million for the third year
news.text: Arrivals crossed 2 million on 20 Nov, three days later than in 2025, after a slump in March and April, so the year is still behind last year's pace despite strong growth from India. A Rs 1.5bn interim promotion drive is rolling out late: UK and Germany campaigns (Rs 100mn each) are awarded, Australia has run since August, and India, China and Russia are in final procurement.

news.title: Asia braces after AI sell-off; US futures bounce
news.text: US stock futures recovered on Monday while Asian markets fell and regional authorities prepared support after last week's sell-off in tech and chip stocks.

news.title: Middle East: new attacks on Saudi Arabia and Bahrain
news.text: Saudi Arabia intercepted a Houthi drone and missile and Bahrain reported an Iranian strike on an industrial site; Iran's foreign minister said the June Islamabad memorandum is off the table but Iran is open to a deal with the US. Tankers were hit near Oman, though oil prices have fallen for three weeks.
